# Plan: Codacy: core/yarn.lock flagged by Lizard file-nloc (false positive on autogenerated lockfile)

Issue: [500-codacy-core-yarn-lock-flagged-by-lizard-file-nloc-false-positive-on-autogenerated-lockfile.md](../../issues/500-codacy-core-yarn-lock-flagged-by-lizard-file-nloc-false-positive-on-autogenerated-lockfile.md)

## Overview
Add `core/yarn.lock` to the repo's `.codacy.yml` `exclude_paths`, following the existing documented-exclusion convention already used for the `core/spec/support/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` entries. This is a single root-level config change with no code impact.

## Context
Codacy's Lizard `file-nloc` complexity check flags `core/yarn.lock` for having 772 non-comment lines — a meaningless signal for a Yarn-autogenerated lockfile. `core/yarn.lock` is confirmed to be the only lockfile in the repo, so this exclusion fully covers the issue with no other paths needed.

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1 — Exclude core/yarn.lock in .codacy.yml
Add `"core/yarn.lock"` to the `exclude_paths` list in `.codacy.yml`, with a comment block above it (matching the file's existing style) explaining that the file is an autogenerated Yarn lockfile and that Lizard's line-count-based complexity check produces a false positive on it, referencing issue #500.

## Files to Change
- `.codacy.yml` — add a new comment block + `"core/yarn.lock"` entry to `exclude_paths`, alongside the existing entries.

## Notes
- No specialist agent owns root-level `.codacy.yml`; this is a single, self-contained config change with no CI job of its own to verify locally (Codacy's own next scan is the only verification, per prior issues #460/#496/#498 handled the same way).
